jobs.title: IN-DOH-NGS Specialist
jobs.location: 550 W 16th St Ste B\nMarion County, Indianapolis, IN 46202
jobs.description:
Purpose of Position/Summary:
Incumbent is responsible for coordinating and performing the full range of molecular biological examinations and analyses, recording, interpreting, and result reporting of tests on specimens which may include human body fluids, tissues (human and animal), isolates from clinical specimens, and environmental samples to the submitting physician, clinic, hospital, or public health agency. Incumbent is also responsible for the development, validation, and implementation of new molecular tests, preparation of validation documents and SOPs, and troubleshooting of the existing molecular tests. Special emphasis for this position will be around genomic sequencing, maintenance of instrumentation for sequencing, and troubleshooting sequencing assays.

Essential Duties/Responsibilities:
Incumbent will have in-depth knowledge and ability in the areas of molecular biology and is able to perform laboratory associated assays or the ability to learn these techniques upon successful completion of proficiency testing. Representative duties include:
• Extraction of nucleic acids from specimens, isolates, and samples via a variety of manual and automated methods;
•Utilize molecular techniques such as, but not limited to, PCR, MALDI-TOF, and NGS;
•Participate in the evaluation, development, validation, and implementation of new testing methods used in clinical/reference laboratory work, as well as, preparation of validation documents and SOPs;
•Provide technical oversight of the daily performance of high complexity testing; strictly following the laboratory's procedures for specimen handling and processing, test analyses, reporting, and maintaining records of test results;
• Maintain laboratory record system of submitted samples and specimens and their possible referral;
• Evaluate, interpret, validate laboratory results, and report findings;
• Conduct quality control checks on laboratory methods, materials, and equipment;
• Document all quality control activities, instrument calibrations, and maintenance performed;
• Participate in evaluation of new products used in clinical/reference laboratory work;
• Perform all related work as required;
•Testing personnel responsibilities (42 CFR 493.1495 Standard):
The testing personnel are responsible for specimen processing, test performance and for reporting test results.
(a) Each individual performs only those high complexity tests that are authorized by the laboratory director and require a degree of skill commensurate with the individual’s education, training or experience, and technical abilities.
(b) Each individual performing high complexity testing must—
(1) Follow the laboratory’s procedures for specimen handling and
processing, test analyses, reporting and maintaining records of patient
test results;
(2) Maintain records that demonstrate that proficiency testing samples are
tested in the same manner as patient specimens;
(3) Adhere to the laboratory’s quality control policies, document all quality
control activities, instrument and procedural calibrations and
maintenance performed;
(4) Follow the laboratory’s established policies and procedures whenever
test systems are not within the laboratory’s established acceptable levels
of performance;
(5) Be capable of identifying problems that may adversely affect test
performance or reporting of test results and either must correct the
problems or immediately notify the general supervisor, technical
supervisor, clinical consultant, or director;
(6) Document all corrective actions taken when test systems deviate from
the laboratory’s established performance specifications; and
(7) Except as specified in paragraph (c) of this section, if qualified under §
493.1489(b)(5), perform high complexity testing only under the onsite,
direct supervision of a general supervisor qualified under § 493.1461.
(c) Exception. For individuals qualified under § 493.1489(b)(5), who were performing
high complexity testing on or before January 19, 1993, the requirements of
paragraph (b)(7) of this section are not effective, provided that all high complexity
testing performed by the individual in the absence of a general supervisor is
reviewed within 24 hours by a general supervisor qualified under § 493.1461

Job Requirements:
• Extensive knowledge of the principles, theories and practices of molecular biology, and related sub- specialties;
• Experience with Next Generation Sequencing platforms, technologies, and procedures.
• Specialized knowledge of current scientific methods and testing procedures and the ability to apply them when seeking solutions to public health laboratory problems;
• Specialized knowledge of and ability to use a full range of standard technical equipment, complex scientific apparatus, and automated techniques of analysis;
• Extensive knowledge of laboratory safety practices and principles;
• Aware of state and federal laws, rules, regulations, and policies concerning the program area (i.e. CLIA);
• Ability to meet requirements for personnel certification as a technologist pursuant to the Clinical Laboratory Improvement Act (CLIA)
• Ability to effectively communicate technical information both verbally and in writing and maintain productive working relationships;
• Ability to satisfactorily participate in proficiency testing programs and recognize QA problems;
• Ability to compile, analyze, evaluate, and prepare laboratory reports.

Supervisory Responsibilities/Direct Reports:
N/A

Difficulty of Work:
Incumbent is engaged in scientific analyses that demand accuracy and demonstrated proficiency in applying laboratory analytical skills to select pertinent guidelines and formulated plans for problem solving. Projects involve many complex variables of great intricacy and the microbiologist is often called upon to analyze and identify unusual specimens/samples. Work requires considerable use of analytical judgement and technical knowledge in order to draw accurate, logical conclusions. Incumbent will also be required to develop and research new testing procedures.

Responsibility:
Incumbent works independently as an expert in the Biothreat laboratory. Technical and/or detailed instruction is provided only upon request when a procedural change and/or special project necessitates it. Incumbent maintains established safety practices when working with materials that have a chemical hazard or biohazard potential. Reports are reviewed for general technical accuracy; however, tasks are performed independently. Errors in work could adversely affect the health, safety and well being of the incumbent or coworkers.

Personal Work Relationships:
Incumbent works with supervisor and with other Department of Health staff such as Laboratory Safety Officer and/or external entities (e.g. local health departments, etc.) to devise and implement work procedures and information dissemination. Individual will have contact with employees and the public as a laboratory expert and in the explanation of laboratory procedures and recommendations when appropriate.

Physical Effort:
The incumbent will be performing tests on potentially dangerous samples (e.g. anthrax). Because of this, safety standards are of primary importance. This position will be required to use all appropriate personal protective equipment in the designated laboratory area.

Working Conditions:
The equipment can be cumbersome and awkward; the laboratory space can experience a dramatic increase in temperature. The incumbent will be required to work in these conditions and maintain a clear thought process during the testing.

Important Note:
This is not a project manager, technical developer, coding, architecture, or IT engineering position. The ideal candidate is a strong communicator with data management experience who can coach, guide, and coordinate stewardship activities.
Enterprise Data Steward Job Description
The Enterprise Data Steward will support VDOT’s Data Program by working directly with assigned data stewards across the agency to strengthen data management practices, improve data quality, and prepare datasets for quality measurement within our data governance tool. In this role, the staff member will facilitate regular meetings with division-level stewards, guide them through required stewardship activities, assist in developing scoping documentation, data dictionaries, and business rules. The staff member will also provide training and hands-on support to build data literacy and stewardship competency. This position serves as the primary liaison between assigned business divisions and the agency’s Data Program, ensuring stewardship activities are well-coordinated, consistent, and aligned with enterprise data quality priorities. The work focuses on coaching, coordination, and applying data management expertise to help stewards prepare their datasets for enterprise data quality measurement.

• Provide training, coaching, and support on data management, data quality concepts, and data stewardship practices.
• Support agencywide data quality and stewardship by providing subject‑area guidance for defining and measuring data quality, collaborating with system owners and SMEs to resolve complex data issues, promoting data literacy and consistent data management practices, and ensuring stewardship activities follow established standards, frameworks, and governance processes.

• Strong understanding of data management principles, data quality concepts, and stewardship processes.
• Ability to communicate clearly verbally and in writing, facilitate group discussions, and guide non-technical staff in data-related work.

Position: Customer Allocations Lead

Duration: 9 Months

Role Summary
The Customer Allocations Lead owns the end-to-end allocation process when customer demand exceeds available supply. This role serves as the central coordination point across Customer Supply Chain, Sales, IDP/Customer Planning, and senior leadership to ensure limited inventory is allocated in a disciplined, transparent, and commercially sound manner.
The role requires a balance of analytical rigor, operational execution, and stakeholder management, ensuring allocations protect strategic customers while minimizing downstream operational risk and organizational friction.
Key Responsibilities
1. Allocation Governance & Decision Support

Own allocation execution in alignment with established RACI and governing principles
Evaluate allocation requests from Sales and Customer Supply Chain when demand exceeds supply
Develop data-backed allocation recommendations for leadership (IDP, CSC, or escalation to USLT)
Ensure allocations remain exception-based and are used sparingly, in line with leadership guidance

2. Analytical Assessment & Scenario Modeling

Analyze demand signals, forecasts, inventory positions, production constraints, and DC availability
Build and maintain allocation models, workbooks, and scenario analyses
Quantify and communicate risks, including:
	
Customer distribution loss
Promotional fill shortfalls
In-stock deterioration
Downstream case fill impacts



3. Execution & System Enablement

Oversee accurate and timely allocation entry in S/4 and related systems
Partner with Order Management and Customer Service for execution alignment
Ensure allocation changes, extensions, and customer-specific adjustments are properly reflected and communicated
Manage allocation timelines (start, extension, and end dates) aligned with production ramps and promotions

4. Cross-Functional Partnership

Act as the central integrator across:
	
Sales (customer advocacy)
Customer Supply Chain (supply constraints)
IDP/Customer Planning (forecast inputs)


Navigate competing priorities using a neutral, data-driven approach
Support leadership forums (CDAs, deep dives, pre-reads) with clear allocation insights and implications

5. Process Improvement & Future State Design

Identify root causes driving allocation needs (forecast gaps, demand spikes, capacity constraints)
Partner cross-functionally to reduce reliance on allocations
Contribute to process simplification, automation, and system improvements
Support training and adoption of allocation processes, templates, and best practices

Key Skills & Capabilities

Strong analytical and financial acumen (demand–supply tradeoff evaluation)
Ability to operate effectively under pressure with senior stakeholders
Deep understanding of customer prioritization and supply chain dynamics
High attention to detail in fast-paced, high-impact decision environments
Excellent written and verbal communication, particularly in escalation scenarios

Quantify and communicate risks, including:

Partner with Order Management and Customer Service for execution alignment

Navigate competing priorities using a neutral, data-driven approach
Support leadership forums (CDAs, deep dives, pre-reads) with clear allocation insights and implications

ENGAGEMENT DESCRIPTION:  

The Care Manager RN leads the coordination of a multidisciplinary team to deliver a holistic, person centric care management program to a diverse health plan population with a variety of health and social needs.  
They serve as the single point of contact for members, caregivers, and providers using a variety of communication channels including phone calls, emails, text messages and the client online messaging platform.  
The Care Manager RN uses the case management process to assess, develop, implement, monitor, and evaluate care plans designed to optimize the member’s health across the care continuum.  
They work in partnership with the member, providers of care and community resources to develop and implement the plan of care and achieve stated goals. 

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES include the following. Other duties may be assigned: 

Lead the coordination of a regionally aligned, multidisciplinary team to provide holistic care to meet member needs telephonic and/or digitally.  
The multidisciplinary team is inclusive of Medical and Behavioral Health Social Workers, Registered Dietitians, Pharmacists, Clinical Support Staff and Medical Directors. 
Use the case management process to assess, develop, implement, monitor, and evaluate care plans designed to optimize the members’ health across the care continuum. 
Assess the member's health, psychosocial needs, cultural preferences, and support systems.  
Engage the member and/or caregiver to develop an individualized plan of care, address barriers, identify gaps in care, and promotes improved overall health outcomes. 
Arrange resources necessary to meet identified needs (e.g., community resources, mental health services, substance abuse services, financial support services and disease-specific services). 
Coordinate care delivery and support among member support systems, including providers, community-based agencies, and family. 
Advocate for members and promote self-advocacy. 
Deliver education to include health literacy, self-management skills, medication plans, and nutrition.  
Monitor and evaluate effectiveness of the care management plan, assess adherence to care plan to ensure progress to goals and adjust and reevaluate as necessary. 
Accurately document interactions that support management of the member. 
Prepare the member and/or caregiver for discharge from a facility to home or for transfer to another healthcare facility to support continuity of care. 
Educate the member and/or caregiver about post-transition care and needed follow-up, summarizing what happened during an episode of care. 
Secure durable medical equipment and transportation services and communicate this to the member and/or caregiver and to key individuals at the receiving facility or home care agency. 
Adhere to professional standards as outlined by protocols, rules and guidelines meeting quality and production goals. 
Continue professional development by completing relevant continuing education and maintaining Certified Case Manager (CCM). 

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:

Nursing Diploma or associate's degree in nursing required. 
Bachelor’s degree in nursing strongly preferred. 
3 years of clinical nursing experience in a clinical, acute/post-acute care, and community setting required. 
1 year of case management experience in a managed care setting strongly preferred. 
Experience managing patients telephonically and via digital channels (mobile applications and messaging) preferred. 

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS:

Current, active, and Licensed RNs that lives in a Compact state and holds a Multistate License. 
Certification in Case Management (CCM) required or to be obtained within 18 months of hire 
Certification in Chronic Care Professional (CCP) preferred QUALIFICATIONS To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily.  
The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required.  
Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. 

OTHER SKILLS AND ABILITIES:

Ability to think critically, be decisive, and problem solve a variety of topics that can impact a member’s outcomes. 
Empathetic, supportive and a good listener. 
Proficient in motivational interviewing skills. 
Demonstrated time management skills. 
Organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple systems/tools, while simultaneously interacting with a member. 
Must have intermediate computer knowledge, typing capability and proficiency in Microsoft programs (Excel, OneNote, Outlook, Teams, Word, etc.). 
Must embrace teamwork but can also work independently. 
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills both written and verbal.

Job Title: Implementation Management

Location: Athens, OH, 45701


Job Type: Temporary Assignment 


Work Type: Onsite   


   


Job Description: 

The Field Performance Advisor (FPA) is responsible for driving optimal performance and continuous improvement among our Suppliers by engaging in regular site visits to consult and engage directly with Suppliers to correct real-time discrepancies and identify ways to improve crew effectiveness, tool utilization, and quality.
The FPA will utilize their knowledge and expertise to consult with Suppliers and develop process improvements that can be integrated across sites and markets throughout the country
The FPA role will partner directly with market Suppliers as a representative of Client to share feedback, recommendations, and work closely with various support groups to implement more efficient and standardized ways of working.

Job Responsibilities  

Review and analyze site performance metrics, including but not limited to, cycle time, close out package (COP) first time right, (Job Hazard Assessment) JHA compliance, client tool utilization, build quality, and customer specific requirements. 
Based on site review and analysis, identify Supplier performance areas in need of improvement, provide feedback on site performance metrics to Territory Director and Suppliers, and partner with Suppliers to correct, adapt, and respond to the feedback. 
Engage with suppliers on-site to conduct root-cause analysis of performance deficiencies, troubleshoot problems, and ensure that Suppliers correct real-time discrepancies related to safety and construction. 
Strategically plan daily and weekly site and supplier visits to achieve key targets and drive overall market performance, considering suppliers’ KPIs, performance, current needs, etc. 
Act as an internal partner for client’s Senior Construction Managers and Project Management teams to review and evaluate market-level on-site requests, such as supporting customer meets, site access, and validating construction drawings, to support in project completion. 
Based on performance metrics, identify, design, and develop process improvements for Supplier’s site construction process, as well as advancements to client tools to increase efficiency and quality, collaborating with the Automation teams to develop new tools and adjust current tools to increase Supplier’s efficiency.
Based on market-level findings, work with other Field Performance Advisors around the country to identify systemic problems and propose cross-market improvements. 
Collect and report on supplier performance data for deployment process changes and new process trials to support business cases for new features or changes to ways of working. 
Build strong relationships with market Suppliers to foster a culture of continuous improvement and two-way feedback between client and Supplier. 
Ensure Suppliers have a clear understanding of, and adhere to, client and customer processes, methods, and tools that apply to sites assigned to Suppliers in market. 
Continuously improve and provide feedback on client and customer specific information and training for accuracy in delivery performance via Site Tracker and Power Bi-domain metrics. 
Support Governance for quarterly Supplier business reviews (QBR), report on findings in the field concerning supplier performance and actions taken and recommendations for improvement; responsible for field-related actions from QBRs.

Behavioral competencies 

Entrepreneurial & innovative thinking. 
Performs at a high level with minimal supervision in a fast paced and fluid work environment. 
Proactively analyzes issues, identifies problems, and makes sound decisions. 
Ability to collaborate and partner with Suppliers for successful delivery. 
Ability to understand performance metrics and analytics and identify areas of improvement. 
Excellent planning & organization skills. 
Strong leadership and consultative skills. 
Strong ability to effectively communicate and work with cross-functional teams, diverse personalities, and professional skill levels. 
Strong verbal and written communication skills. 
Advocates and generates a positive work environment and culture that embodies client’s core values.

Typical Interfaces Internal: 

Market Project Team 
Customer Unit (CU) 
Customer Project Management 
Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) 
Client Automation and Operational Excellence team 

People Function External: 

Customers 
Third Party Suppliers Qualifications and Experiences 
Minimum relevant work/industry experience of 7+ years. 
Bachelor’s degree preferred. 
Experience with providing design solutions and guidance on order of operations. 
Strong knowledge of general construction processes & procedures. 
Experience in managing and directing general contractor suppliers, construction scope estimation, etc. (Civils, Ground, L&A, Backhaul, Maintenance Work). 
Knowledge of and ability to enforce client and customer construction and quality standards. 
Ability to interface with customers, property owners, and other internal and external ancillary personnel as needed. 
Strong knowledge of contracts (leasing, vendor facing, customer facing) and financial acumen. 
Demonstrated ability to collaborate and develop positive relationships with suppliers or other external business partners. 
Experience leading or influencing teams to perform at their best. 
Strong understanding of applicable health and safety regulations impacting client and its suppliers in the local market. 
Completion of approved OSHA (Occupational Safety and Health Administration) 30-hour course for telecommunications industry. 
Previous experience working on client equipment portfolio is a plus.

Job Title: Cloud Architect 
Location: Lansing, MI 48933 
Duration: 6 Months   
Job Type: Hybrid 
Work Type: Temporary Assignment 
Shift: 8.00AM - 5.00 PM 
  
Job Description:   

We are seeking a Senior Cloud Migration Architect to embed with our development team and lead the AWS platform configuration and CI/CD automation for a large-scale enterprise cloud migration program.
The program covers 30+ applications across migration approaches such as Elastic Beanstalk, Amazon EKS, EC2/Cloud VM - to be delivered across multiple sprints. 
The contractor will own the technical configuration of AWS services for each migration pattern, design and build Azure DevOps (ADO) pipelines that integrate with ArgoCD or Flux for GitOps-driven deployments to EKS, and partner closely with application teams, the AWS Infrastructure Team, and the DBA team to deliver production-ready environments sprint by sprint. 
This is a hands-on, deeply technical role for someone who can move fast, write production-grade IaC, debug across the stack, and mentor application developers and administrators on cloud-native patterns. 

Key Responsibilities 
 
AWS Platform Configuration 

Configure and tune AWS Elastic Beanstalk environments for applications across Dev, Test, and Prod, including platform versions, scaling policies, environment variables, and rolling deployment configuration 
Stand up and operate Amazon EKS clusters across Dev/Test/Prod for containerized workloads, including node groups, cluster autoscaling, ingress controllers, and namespace strategy 
Provision and harden EC2/Cloud VM environments, including AMI selection, instance sizing, OS-level configuration, and patching strategy 
Partner with the DBA team on Amazon RDS setup for SQL Server and PostgreSQL including parameter groups, subnet groups, backup policies, and Multi-AZ configuration 
Design VPC networking, security groups, IAM roles/policies, KMS keys, and Secrets Manager integration following least-privilege principles 
Build infrastructure-as-code (Terraform preferred; CloudFormation acceptable) so every environment is reproducible and auditable 

CI/CD & GitOps 

Design and build Azure DevOps build and release pipelines tailored to each migration pattern:  
EB pattern: source build → artifact → eb deploy to environment per stage 
EKS pattern: Docker build → ECR push → manifest/Helm chart update → GitOps sync via ArgoCD or Flux 
EC2 pattern: build → AMI bake or aws-deploy → blue/green or rolling release 
In-place upgrade pattern: validation, packaging, and controlled deployment to existing servers 
Implement GitOps using ArgoCD or Flux for EKS workloads - pull-based deployments, automated drift detection, app-of-apps or kustomize/helm patterns, multi-cluster or multi-namespace promotion 
Establish promotion strategy across Dev to Test to Prod with appropriate gates, approvals, and rollback mechanisms 
Standardize pipeline templates (YAML) so application teams can self-onboard new services consistently 
Integrate static analysis, container scanning (Trivy/ECR scan), SAST/DAST hooks, and artifact provenance into the pipeline 

Observability & Reliability 

Configure CloudWatch logs, metrics, alarms, and dashboards for each workload 
Define SLOs, alerting thresholds, and incident response runbooks for production cutover events 

Documentation & Hand-off 


Produce architecture decision records (ADRs), runbooks, and operational procedures so workloads can be supported by the long-term operations team  


Maintain a clean, versioned IaC repository as the source of truth for all environments 


Collaboration 


Work daily with application development teams, AWS Infrastructure Team, DBA Team, and Tech Leads 


Pair with developers to debug cloud-specific issues (cold starts, container OOMs, RDS connectivity, IAM denials) 


Required Qualifications 


5–6+ years hands-on experience building and operating production workloads on AWS, with deep knowledge of Elastic Beanstalk, EKS, EC2, RDS, VPC, IAM, S3, CloudWatch, and Secrets Manager 


3+ years hands-on with Kubernetes - production EKS preferred, including Helm, kubectl, ingress (ALB/NGINX), HPA, and troubleshooting pods/services/networking 


Production experience with ArgoCD or Flux - designed app-of-apps structure, managed multi-environment promotion, and resolved GitOps drift in real workloads. This is non-negotiable. 


Strong Azure DevOps Pipelines (YAML) experience - build pipelines, multi-stage release pipelines, variable groups, service connections, and self-hosted/Microsoft-hosted agents. Equivalent strong experience in another major CI/CD tool (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins) is acceptable if Azure DevOps can be picked up quickly 


Solid Docker skills - multi-stage builds, image hardening, ECR 


Infrastructure-as-Code in production: Terraform (preferred) or CloudFormation/CDK 


Database familiarity - comfortable working with DBA teams on RDS (SQL Server and PostgreSQL), connection strings, secrets rotation, and migration cutover 


Linux administration (RHEL/Amazon Linux/Ubuntu) and shell scripting (bash) 


Source control with Git - branching strategies, pull requests, code review discipline 


Strong written communication - must produce clear runbooks, architecture diagrams, and PR descriptions 


Preferred Qualifications 


AWS certifications: AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Professional or DevOps Engineer - Professional 


CKA / CKAD (Certified Kubernetes Administrator/Developer) 


Experience migrating .NET and Java applications from on-premises to AWS 


Experience operating COTS products in containerized or cloud environments 


Experience with service mesh (Istio, App Mesh) or API gateways

The Program Management Office (PMO) sits within the IDC and is responsible for ensuring our highest-priority campaigns and programs are delivered on time and to an extremely high quality.

Role description:

Our Program Managers provide dedicated Agile and program management support to IDC functions. 
In this role, you will facilitate sprint planning and execution, maintain shared campaign roadmaps, and manage delivery interlocks across functions to ensure alignment with IDC and IDP priorities.
As an Integrated Demand Plan (IDP) Program Manager, we count on you to provide the structure, discipline, and momentum to deliver an IDP against Client's goals and objectives. 
You are an advocate of campaign process and the predictor of hiccups before they happen. 
As an IDP Program Manager, you should be the best dot-connector on the planet, keeping stakeholders regularly in the loop through Agile methods and coaching. 
You are responsible for onboarding the IDP team into Agile ways of working, setting up and managing the team’s Agile rhythm, identifying and escalating blockers, facilitating the Agile Ceremonies, and coaching the team to improve. 
You will act as a whole-lifecycle thinker to ensure every angle is covered as efficiently as possible. 
Passion for working with cross-functional teams to deliver results is a must. 
You should be able to demonstrate the ability to work backwards, starting with customers, stakeholders, and any related team owners

Key responsibilities:

Utilize Agile methodologies to deliver the creation and execution of an IDP

Continuously improve delivery processes and identify opportunities for operational54 efficiency, with a keen eye on opportunities to accelerate through standardization,55 automation, and AI

 
IDP Program Manager II (L5) and Program Manager III (L6) alignment:

The role and responsibilities are the same between Program Manager II (L5) and III (L6). The level differs in terms of the scope, influence, and complexity of the IDP to which they are assigned. 
IDP PM roles for our most complex IDPs that include multiple campaigns, large customer segments and stakeholder base, and extensive ambiguity are scoped as Program Manager III (L6), whereas all other IDP PM roles are scoped as Program Manager II (L5). 
Roles that include a less complex IDP and another critical area of responsibility (e.g. Agile coaching) are scoped as Program Manager III (L6).

Position: Project/Program Manager II

Work Type: Onsite
 
Overview:

The Client Integrated Demand Center (IDC) is reimagining global demand generation. Collectively the team develops and implements Integrated Demand Plans (IDPs) that align with Client's business priorities and enable fast and iterative time-to-market, improved customer engagement, and delivery to Client business goals. 
The Program Management Office (PMO) sits within the IDC and is responsible for ensuring our highest-priority campaigns and programs are delivered on time and to an extremely high quality. 
Our PMO team works across key IDC functions including Integrated Demand Planning, Digital and Channel Execution, Content and Asset Management, Performance & Analytics, Customer Experience, and Lead Management with the goal of creating a more consistent, cohesive, and relevant customer journey across Client's global marketing efforts.
As a Program Manager within the IDC's PMO, you will serve as the heartbeat of our global marketing initiatives, orchestrating cross-functional collaboration and delivery. 
You excel at removing ambiguity, creating structured approaches that enable teams to move quickly while maintaining quality standards, and championing meaningful impact over activity metrics. 
You are responsible for establishing clear execution frameworks, adapting processes based on team needs, and driving continuous improvement in how the IDC operates. 
This role requires you to balance the need for standardization with flexibility, while consistently driving high-impact outcomes that advance18 Client's marketing objectives.

Role description:

Our Program Managers provide dedicated Agile and program management support to IDC functions. 
In this role, you will facilitate sprint planning and execution, maintain shared campaign roadmaps, and manage delivery interlocks across functions to ensure alignment with IDC and IDP priorities.
As an Integrated Demand Plan (IDP) Program Manager, we count on you to provide the structure, discipline, and momentum to deliver an IDP against Client's goals and objectives. 
You are an advocate of campaign process and the predictor of hiccups before they happen. 
As an IDP Program Manager, you should be the best dot-connector on the planet, keeping stakeholders regularly in the loop through Agile methods and coaching. 
You are responsible for onboarding the IDP team into Agile ways of working, setting up and managing the team’s Agile rhythm, identifying and escalating blockers, facilitating the Agile Ceremonies, and coaching the team to improve. 
You will act as a whole-lifecycle thinker to ensure every angle is covered as efficiently as possible. 
Passion for working with cross-functional teams to deliver results is a must. 
You should be able to demonstrate the ability to work backwards, starting with customers, stakeholders, and any related team owners

Key responsibilities:

Utilize Agile methodologies to deliver the creation and execution of an IDP
Operate as part of an IDP Core Team, partnering with functional leads to ensure requirements, timelines, and outputs remain aligned to business outcomes
Lead Agile ceremonies and develop consistency in work prioritization and backlog Management
Maintain shared roadmaps and manage cross-functional delivery interlocks, owning program status reports and delivery dashboards
Utilize and operate waterfall workbacks in Workfront and collaborative workstream46 operations within Figma
Coordinate inputs to set up workstream kickoffs
Lead and consolidate sprint retrospectives across Core IDP team and analyze for future49 process efficiencies
Identify project risks and implement performance tracking and measurement protocols
Own documentation, artifacts, templates, and standard operating procedures (SOPs), ensuring consistency across all event teams
Continuously improve delivery processes and identify opportunities for operational54 efficiency, with a keen eye on opportunities to accelerate through standardization,55 automation, and AI

 
IDP Program Manager II (L5) and Program Manager III (L6) alignment:

The role and responsibilities are the same between Program Manager II (L5) and III (L6). The level differs in terms of the scope, influence, and complexity of the IDP to which they are assigned. 
IDP PM roles for our most complex IDPs that include multiple campaigns, large customer segments and stakeholder base, and extensive ambiguity are scoped as Program Manager III (L6), whereas all other IDP PM roles are scoped as Program Manager II (L5). 
Roles that include a less complex IDP and another critical area of responsibility (e.g. Agile coaching) are scoped as Program Manager III (L6).

Required qualifications for this role include:

Program management experience (3+ years for PM II, 6+ years for PM III)
Marketing or digital campaign experience (3+ years for PM II, 6+ years for PM III)
Experience leading Agile ceremonies
Workfront training and certification (certification can be obtained in the role)
Agile training and certification (certification can be obtained in the role)

IDP Core team’s progression in Agile maturity, with the expectation to improve one step each year
On-time or early delivery of annual IDP and quarterly updates
On-time or early delivery of IDP bill of materials (BOM) and activations

Compose requests/responses for downstream systems based on business rules

Work Type: Hybrid 
 
Job Description: 


Under broad supervision, analyzes customer business needs and participates in the planning, design and implementation of new or enhanced systems. 


May act as a team or project leader.


The Instructional Designer is responsible for developing innovative instructional programs and materials that align with organizational goals and learner needs for the State Accounting Office (SAO). This role requires a blend of instructional design expertise, creativity, and strong communication skills to create engaging and effective learning experiences. 


The Instructional Designer will collaborate with subject matter experts (SMEs) and stakeholders to ensure the accuracy and relevancy of training content. 


Key Responsibilities:


Conduct thorough Training Needs Assessments and Audience Analyses to identify learning objectives and performance gaps, training participants, and delivery channels. 


Design,  develop and maintains comprehensive, 508-compliant instructional materials, including course summary sheets, learning objectives, course outlines, storyboards, video scripts, job aids, quick reference sheets, and other supporting documents for training deliverables. 


Create online, interactive training materials in various formats, such as printable job aids, instructor-led (virtual and in-person), microlearning, videos, and eLearning courses. 


Generate program interactive, SCORM-compliant webinars, microlearning and full-length eLearning courses in eLearning authoring tools (e.g., Articulate Storyline,  Adobe Captivate, Camtasia)


Develop and administer a variety of assessments, including quizzes, tests, simulations, and practical exercises, to measure learner progress and comprehension. Analyze assessment data to evaluate the effectiveness of instructional programs, identify areas for improvement, and make data-driven recommendations for enhancing learning outcomes.


Accurately track and document the progress of instructional design projects, ensuring milestones and deadlines are met. Utilize project management tools to monitor timelines, resource allocation, and deliverables, and provide regular updates to stakeholders on the status of development efforts.


Collaborate with subject matter experts (SMEs) to gather content and ensure the accuracy and relevancy of learning materials. Work closely with stakeholders, including leadership teams and learners, to understand learning needs and objectives, ensuring that training programs align with organizational goals and learner requirements.


Periodically review and update curriculum and existing training content to ensure accuracy, relevancy and alignment with organizational goals and industry standards.


Stay current with industry trends and best practices in instructional design and adult learning theory.


Performs other duties as assigned by management.


Qualifications:


Minimum of 3-5 years of experience in Instructional Design, Education, Training and Development, or a related field. 


Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (e.g. Word, PowerPoint, Excel).


Proficiency in eLearning authoring tools (e.g. Articulate Storyline, Adobe Captivate, Camtasia).


Experience with instructional design methodologies (e.g. ADDIE, Kirkpatrick’s Level of assessments, adult learning principles)


Experience with SCORM-compliant course development and Learning Management Systems (LMS)


Strong understanding of 508-compliance requirements and best practices for creating accessible learning materials.


Expertise in designing and developing comprehensive instructional materials, including course summary sheets, learning objectives, course outlines, storyboards, video scripts, job aids, quick reference sheets, and other supporting documents.


Ability to create online, interactive training materials in various formats, such as printable job aids, instructor-led (virtual and in-person), microlearning, videos, and eLearning courses.


Experience in developing and administering a variety of assessments and analyzing assessment data to evaluate instructional program effectiveness.

Job Description:

jobs.description:
Overview:

As a global leader in serving the scientific community, the organization generates approximately $40 billion in annual revenue and is committed to making the world healthier, cleaner, and safer. Their global team delivers innovative technologies, convenient procurement solutions, and pharmaceutical services through industry-leading brands.
Position:         Manufacturing Operator
Location:        Detroit, MI 48201
Duration:        3 Months
Job Type:       Contract
Work Type:    Onsite

Summary:
The Manufacturing Operator plays a key role in the production of animal-origin peptones within a manufacturing environment. Collaborate with supervisors and team members to maintain efficient production flow.

High school diploma or equivalent preferred.
Ability to work in a manufacturing environment with exposure to chemicals and raw animal-origin materials.
Comfortable working in environments with strong odors.
Ability to follow detailed instructions and safety procedures.
Strong attention to detail and documentation accuracy.
Ability to operate pallet jacks and material handling equipment.
Team-oriented with strong communication skills.
Routine exposure to chemicals and animal-origin raw materials.
Exposure to strong odors associated with manufacturing processes.
Required PPE includes safety glasses, steel-toe boots, hair nets, and beard nets where applicable.
Additional PPE such as Tyvek suits, face shields, lab coats, and protective gloves may be required depending on tasks performed.

jobs.description:
Overview:   


         


TekWissen is a global workforce management provider headquartered in Ann Arbor, Michigan that offers strategic talent solutions to our clients world-wide. Our client provider of digital technology and transformation, information technology and services    


            


Position: Data Engineer  


Location: Parsippany, NJ; Frisco, TX; Overland Park, KS; Bellevue, WA 


Duration: 6 Months 


Job Type: Temporary Assignment   


Work Type: Hybrid 


 


Job Description  



We are seeking a hands-on Data Engineer or Associate Data Engineer with strong programming skills in Python and SQL and practical experience building scalable data ingestion, transformation, and quality pipelines using Azure ecosystem. 
This role will focus on building scalable ingestion pipelines into the Bronze layer, developing Silver and Gold layer patterns, with strong focus on data quality, and enabling governed semantic models through Microsoft Fabric for analytics and reporting. 

Key Responsibilities 

Implement medallion lakehouse architecture patterns across Bronze, Silver, and Gold layers. 
Build and maintain ingestion pipelines that bring structured, semi-structured data, files, API sources into the Bronze layer of the lakehouse. 
Develop Silver layer patterns focused on data cleaning, standardization, deduplication, validation, and business-rule application. 
Develop Gold layer datasets that are curated, analytics-ready, and suitable for enterprise reporting and semantic model consumption. 
Build reliable data pipelines using Azure Databricks, SQL, and Python. 
Design and support orchestration workflows using Azure Data Factory Implement data quality checks, reconciliation logic, exception handling, and monitoring across pipelines. 
Support enterprise data warehouse design, including dimensional modeling, star schemas, fact tables, and dimension tables. 
Prepare curated datasets that support semantic models, governed reporting, dashboards, and business intelligence use cases. 
Enable semantic layers and semantic models through Microsoft Fabric, including Fabric Lakehouse, Fabric Warehouse, OneLake, and Power BI semantic model integration. Optimize data pipelines, transformations, models, and processing jobs for performance, scalability, and maintainability. 
Collaborate with data analysts, BI developers, business stakeholders, and platform teams to translate requirements into trusted, reusable data products. 
Communicate technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. 

Required Skills and Experience 

Data Engineer 3-5 years of industry experience in data engineering, analytics engineering and enterprise data platforms Strong hands-on experience with SQL and Python for data pipeline development, transformation, validation, and performance optimization. 
Experience building ingestion pipelines into a lakehouse, cloud data platform, or enterprise data warehouse. 
Experience designing and implementing Bronze, Silver, and Gold layers in a medallion lakehouse architecture. 
Hands-on experience with Azure Databricks and distributed data processing. 
Experience with Snowflake, including data loading, transformation, performance tuning, and integration with cloud platforms. 
Experience implementing data cleaning, standardization, deduplication, validation, reconciliation, and data quality rules. 
Working experience with enterprise data warehouses, dimensional modeling, star schemas, fact tables, and dimension tables. 
Hands on experience with Microsoft Fabric a plus Experience creating curated datasets for reporting, analytics, dashboards, and semantic model consumption. 
Understanding of data governance, metadata management, lineage, monitoring, and production support best practices. 
Ability to own specific data domains, act as a subject matter expert, and guide implementation patterns. 

Preferred Qualifications 

Azure, Microsoft Fabric, Databricks, or Snowflake certification preferred. 
Experience with Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, OneLake, or similar lakehouse governance technologies. 
Experience implementing reusable ingestion, Silver transformation, and Gold curation patterns. 
Experience supporting Power BI or Microsoft Fabric semantic model development. 
Experience building production-grade data pipelines for enterprise analytics, reporting, or data platform modernization. 

Technical Skills: 

Python, SQL, PySpark, Pandas, Azure Databricks, Azure Data Factory, Snowflake, Star Schema, Dimensional Modeling and Microsoft Fabric.

jobs.description:
Position Title: Senior IT Business Analyst
Location: San Jose, CA Hybrid
Duration: 6+ Months
Role Overview
Client IT Application team is seeking a seasoned Senior Business Analyst to serve as the vital link between our business stakeholders and technical teams. You won’t just be writing requirements; you will be the "owner" of the project lifecycle for smaller, high-impact initiatives. The ideal candidate is as comfortable facilitating a discovery workshop with executives as they are performing UAT (User Acceptance Testing) alongside developers to ensure a bug-free release. This candidate will also drive enterprise AI enablement by developing adoption strategies, mastering prompt engineering, and delivering workshops.

Stakeholder Management & Requirements:

Lead discovery sessions to elicit, translate, and document complex business needs into clear technical specifications (User Stories, PRDs, and Process Maps).
Manage stakeholder expectations and provide regular updates on project health.
Map current ("as-is") and design future ("to-be") business processes
Work with business leaders to define project scope and objectives
Facilitate regular meetings across stakeholders to ensure alignment on project goals and progress.


Technical Partnership & Quality Assurance:

Collaborate daily with developers to clarify requirements and remove blockers.
Assist the engineering team by defining acceptance criteria and performing functional testing to ensure the "Definition of Done" is met.
Identify and document edge cases that stakeholders might have missed.


Project Leadership:

Act as a de-facto Project Manager for smaller workstreams, ensuring milestones are met on time and within scope.
Prioritize the backlog based on business value and technical feasibility.


AI Adoption, Training and Enablement:

Create and disseminate clear documentation, best practices, workshops, and training materials to help employees get the most value out of the available AI tools.

Develop Expertise in Prompt Engineering: Master the skill of writing effective prompts to get desired results from GenAI tools and train others to do the same.
Foster a Culture of Learning: Promote a culture of continuous learning by creating AI adoption communities and making the successes of early adopters highly visible.

·       Experience: 5+ years of experience in Business Analysis, with a proven track record of supporting the full SDLC. Experience with Agile or hybrid project methodologies. Strong understanding of AI platforms, conversational interfaces, and enterprise knowledge systems.

Tools: Proficiency in ServiceNow, SharePoint, Confluence, and wireframing tools (e.g., Lucidchart, Figma, or Miro), GenAI tools (e.g. Gemini, ChatGPT, or Copilot)
Mindset: A "get-it-done" attitude with the ability to pivot between strategic thinking and tactical execution.

The ideal candidate will have experience in SAP S/4HANA Finance, SAP DRC configuration, EMEA e-Invoicing compliance, XML/JSON message handling, SAP integrations, and regulatory reporting solutions, along with a passion for enterprise digital transformation and compliance automation.
Job Title: SAP DRC Consultant
Location: New Jersey, NJ (Remote)
Duration: 6 Months (Can Extend)
Job Description:
Trilyon is seeking an experienced SAP DRC Consultant to support SAP DRC e-Invoicing implementation and compliance initiatives for global enterprise environments. The SAP DRC Consultant will be responsible for designing, configuring, and implementing SAP DRC eDocument Framework solutions to support country-specific statutory and tax compliance requirements. The SAP DRC Consultant will work closely with finance teams, tax stakeholders, business users, and technical teams to ensure successful deployment and support of SAP Digital Reporting Compliance solutions.
The SAP DRC Consultant will support end-to-end e-Invoicing and statutory reporting processes including document generation, validation, submission, monitoring, and reporting activities. The SAP DRC Consultant will also manage integration activities across SAP FI, SD, and MM modules while ensuring compliance with EMEA regulations including France and Germany e-Invoicing frameworks. The ideal SAP DRC Consultant will possess strong SAP Finance expertise, integration knowledge, and the ability to manage compliance-focused SAP implementations within complex enterprise environments.

• Design and configure SAP DRC eDocument Framework solutions for country-specific compliance requirements.
• Implement end-to-end e-Invoicing and statutory reporting processes including document generation, validation, submission, and status monitoring.
• Configure SAP DRC cockpit, mappings, validations, and document formats according to local and regional regulatory requirements.
• Translate legal and tax mandates into SAP DRC functional configurations and compliance workflows.
• Support compliance requirements such as real-time clearance, clearance-based invoicing, periodic reporting, and archival processes.
• Monitor and track regulatory changes while ensuring timely SAP system updates and compliance adjustments.
• Ensure seamless integration of SAP DRC with SAP FI, SD, and MM processes.
• Support integrations with government platforms using SAP BTP and SAP Integration Suite where applicable.
• Analyze and resolve XML, JSON, AIF monitoring, and message-processing issues.
• Support SIT, UAT, Mock Runs, Cutover, Go-Live, and Hypercare activities.
• Perform issue analysis, defect resolution, and coordination with SAP OSS support teams.
• Provide post Go-Live support, production stabilization, and troubleshooting assistance.
• Prepare and maintain functional specifications, configuration documentation, and compliance-related documentation.
• Conduct user training sessions and provide knowledge transfer support to business and technical teams.
• Collaborate with business stakeholders, tax teams, vendors, and project teams to ensure successful project delivery.
Required Skills & Experience:
• Strong experience with SAP S/4HANA or SAP ECC Finance modules including FI, AR, AP, VAT, and Tax.
• Hands-on experience with SAP DRC eDocument Framework configuration and implementation.
• Experience implementing e-Invoicing and e-Reporting solutions.
• Strong knowledge of XML and JSON message handling processes.
• Experience with AIF (Application Interface Framework) monitoring and issue resolution.
• Experience supporting end-to-end testing activities including SIT and UAT.
• Strong understanding of SAP integrations, statutory compliance, and localization requirements.
• Experience supporting SAP compliance reporting and government platform integrations.
• Strong communication, documentation, and stakeholder management skills.
• Ability to work independently and collaboratively in enterprise SAP environments.
Preferred Skills:
• Experience supporting SAP DRC implementations within the EMEA region.
• Experience with France e-Invoicing frameworks including Chorus Pro and PDP model integrations.
• Experience with Germany e-Invoicing standards including XRechnung and ZUGFeRD frameworks.
• Experience with SAP BTP and SAP Integration Suite integrations.
• Familiarity with SAP OSS support coordination and issue escalation processes.
• Experience supporting global statutory reporting and localization initiatives.
• Knowledge of tax regulations, digital invoicing standards, and government compliance mandates.

• Integrate automation with versioned benchmark configurations, scripts, and artifacts.

• Manage Linux-based environments optimized for CPU performance testing.
• Containerize services using Docker and orchestrate environments using Kubernetes where applicable.

• Monitor platform health, benchmark execution, and infrastructure using observability tools.
• Troubleshoot automated benchmark failures, identify root causes, and apply fixes or workarounds.
• Perform capacity planning and scale systems to support increasing benchmark demand.

• Process and structure benchmark data using Python, Spark, or Databricks.
• Support reporting dashboards and analytics tools such as Power BI to deliver performance insights.
Collaboration & Documentation:
• Work closely with CPU performance engineers to improve automation workflows and platform efficiency.

• Engage with external stakeholders and present technical findings when needed.

• Strong understanding of Linux systems, OS tuning, and server environments.
• Experience automating infrastructure using Ansible or similar tools.

Snowflake / Oracle / Python

Collaborate with cross-functional teams to design fault-tolerant, resilient systems with automated failover and recovery. 
Optimize cloud resource usage and cost through rightsizing and autoscaling configurations. 
Automate operational tasks and incident response using scripting and infrastructure as code (Terraform, CloudFormation). 
Maintain detailed documentation of system architecture, deployment processes, and operational runbooks.

Field Quality & Performance Management Coordinate coverage and onsite experience for new customer launchers in your hub Conduct on-the-job evaluations of OSS during live shifts Provide direct feedback and coaching to improve performance Identify high performers and underperformers; take appropriate action
4. Market Development & Ad Hoc Operations Support local growth efforts, including: Treat drop-offs for new customers Visiting prospective restaurant partners Test orders from restaurants to maintain quality standards Act as the on-the-ground representative of operations in your region 
5. Ownership of Hub Performance Maintain a strong, reliable OSS bench for your hub Ensure coverage, quality, and readiness for all shifts in your region Partner with Shift Leads and central ops to flag gaps or risks What Good Looks Like Great customer onsite experience and order quality in your hub Strong pipeline of high-quality OSS in your region New hires ramp quickly and perform at a high level Consistent execution quality across all shifts in your hub Clear visibility into OSS performance and gaps Local operations feel “tight” and well-managed

2–5 years in operations, field management, recruiting, or training roles
Strong people judgment — can identify high vs. low performers quickly Comfortable giving direct feedback and coaching in the field

Job Title: NIST Assessor Lead

NIST SP 800‑171 Assessment – NIST Assessor
Position Overview
The NIST SP 800‑171 Assessor is responsible for planning, conducting, and documenting cybersecurity risk and compliance assessments aligned to NIST SP 800‑171 requirements. The assessor evaluates the effectiveness of security controls protecting Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), identifies gaps, quantifies risk, and develops prioritized remediation recommendations. This role works closely with institutional IT, security, legal, and leadership stakeholders and may support broader governance, risk management, and incident response initiatives.


Key Responsibilities
NIST SP 800‑171 Risk Assessment

Lead and execute NIST SP 800‑171 assessments in accordance with NIST guidelines, institutional policies, and contractual or regulatory requirements.
Review system boundaries, data flows, and environments that store, process, or transmit Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI).
Evaluate the implementation and effectiveness of NIST SP 800‑171 security controls across all 14 control families, including access control, incident response, system integrity, and risk assessment.
Conduct interviews, technical reviews, evidence validation, and control testing to assess compliance and maturity.

Risk Identification & Analysis

Identify security gaps, weaknesses, and vulnerabilities impacting the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of sensitive data.
Assess and prioritize cybersecurity risks based on likelihood, impact, and business context.
Quantify top risks in a manner understandable to both technical teams and executive leadership.

Reporting & Deliverables

Develop clear, well‑structured assessment deliverables, including: 

Detailed NIST SP 800‑171 findings and gap analysis
A prioritized risk register with actionable remediation strategies
Executive‑level findings summaries and post‑assessment memoranda


Present assessment results, conclusions, and recommendations to stakeholders, including senior leadership and governance bodies.
Ensure reports are suitable for ongoing institutional use and future reassessments.

Collaboration & Advisory Support

Work collaboratively with IT, security, compliance, and business stakeholders to validate findings and recommendations.
Provide subject‑matter expertise on NIST, risk management, and cybersecurity best practices, especially in higher education or public sector environments.
Participate in risk workshops and planning discussions as part of broader cybersecurity governance initiatives.
Support alignment between cybersecurity objectives and overall organizational mission and risk tolerance.



Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field (or equivalent experience).
Hands‑on experience conducting NIST SP 800‑171 assessments, audits, or compliance reviews.
Strong understanding of: 

NIST SP 800‑171 and NIST SP 800‑53 control frameworks
Risk management principles and methodologies
Information security governance and compliance


Experience developing professional assessment reports, risk registers, and executive‑level summaries.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to explain technical issues to non‑technical audiences.



Preferred Qualifications

Experience in higher education, government, or regulated public‑sector environments.
Familiarity with SUNY or similar large, distributed academic institutions.
Experience supporting incident response activities or tabletop exercises.
Knowledge of other cybersecurity frameworks and regulations (e.g., NIST CSF, ISO 27001, CJIS, HIPAA, FERPA).



Certifications (Preferred)

CISSP, CISA, or CISM
NIST‑related certification (e.g., NIST RMF, NIST 800‑171 training/certificate)
CRISC or similar risk‑focused certification



Core Competencies

Risk‑based thinking and analytical judgment
Attention to detail and evidence‑based assessment
Stakeholder engagement and facilitation
Documentation and reporting excellence
Ethical judgment and confidentiality



Work Environment & Engagement

May be part of a multi‑year cybersecurity engagement.
Collaborates with virtual and on‑site teams.
Supports recurring assessments, updates, and continuous improvement initiatives.

This individual will primarily work to expand our capabilities supporting the Controlled Substance and Monitoring Database (CSMD), Tennessee’s Prescription Drug Monitoring Program (PDMP) data. We are seeking a skilled and analytical professional to join our public health surveillance and prevention team as an Epidemiologist focused on prescription data. The epidemiologist will collect, manage, and analyze data related to prescription drug use, misuse, and overdose to support evidence-based public health responses. Perform statistical analysis to identify trends, hotspots, and risk factors for drug overdose.
Create dashboards and reports for internal and external stakeholders.
Work with epidemiologists, program managers, and healthcare providers to inform prevention and intervention efforts.
Ensure data quality, security, and conﬁdentiality in line with HIPAA, applicable data governance policies and other regulations.
Contribute to grant applications, research studies, and presentations as needed.

Master’s degree in public health, Epidemiology, Biostatistics, Data Science, or related ﬁeld.

Proﬁciency in analytical and visualization tools (e.g., R, SAS, Stata, Python, and Tableau).
Strong SQL skills and familiarity with relational databases.
Experience linking different datasets.
Ability to communicate complex data ﬁndings to non-technical audiences.
Knowledge of public health data sources and overdose surveillance systems.

The Salesforce Solutions Architect serves as a senior-level technical resource responsible for Salesforce architecture guidance, solution governance, security review, integration alignment, data governance, and enterprise modernization support across the State of OhioDepartment of Developmental Disabilities enterprise. This position requires deep hands-on expertise across Salesforce GovCloud, Salesforce platform architecture, Experience Cloud, Public Sector Solutions, Apex, Lightning Web Components, Salesforce Flow, data modeling, sharing and visibility, DevOps, integrations, and enterprise data platforms. The consultant will operate as a strategic partner and technical authority, collaborating extensively with Enterprise Architecture, Application Development, Cybersecurity, Infrastructure, Database Administration, Integration, Product, and Production Support teams to ensure Salesforce solutions align with agency mission, security standards, compliance needs, and long-term platform sustainability. The selected candidate will help the Enterprise Architecture team review solution designs, identify technical risks, recommend scalable patterns, prevent technical debt, and support complex initiatives such as Salesforce GovCloud implementation, Public Sector Solutions licensing impacts, data masking, Data 360 / Data Cloud planning, and cross-application dependency management. ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS & RESPONSIBILITIES Salesforce Architecture, Platform Governance & Solution Design (40%) Provide Salesforce architecture guidance for applications built on Salesforce GovCloud and related Salesforce platform capabilities. Guide teams on the appropriate use of standard Salesforce objects, custom objects, shared objects, record types, permission sets, profiles, sharing rules, Salesforce Flow, Apex, Lightning Web Components, validation rules, custom metadata, custom settings, APIs, and Experience Cloud. Review and recommend technical designs for new Salesforce applications, enhancements, integrations, automations, data flows, and cross-application dependencies. Evaluate whether proposed solutions are scalable, secure, maintainable, supportable, and aligned with Department enterprise standards. Help prevent unnecessary object proliferation and promote reuse of common enterprise objects, shared services, reusable patterns, and standard architecture practices. Support technical decision-making around common Salesforce data structures such as Account, Contact, Account Contact Relationship, provider relationships, individual records, assessments, files, county board relationships, cases, and related data models. Document architecture decisions, diagrams, risks, dependencies, assumptions, tradeoffs, and recommendations in a leadership-friendly format. Cross-Team Collaboration, Technical Leadership & Delivery Support (25%) Participate in architecture reviews, refinement sessions, sprint planning, technical design discussions, production support discussions, and release readiness reviews. 1 Partner with Application Development, Cybersecurity, Infrastructure, Database Administration, Integration, Help Desk, Product, and Production Support teams to align Salesforce solutions with enterprise architecture direction. 1 Provide recommendations around DevOps, deployment sequencing, sandbox strategy, release management, regression testing, and post-deployment validation. 1 Support code review guidance for Apex, Lightning Web Components, Salesforce Flow, integrations, configuration, and shared services. 1 Help evaluate performance risks including governor limits, DML limits, heap size, CPU time, record locking, sharing recalculation, data volume, asynchronous processing, and batch processing constraints. 1 Research upcoming Salesforce platform, security, licensing, and enterprise architecture changes and communicate opportunities and risks through the enterprise. 1 Provide technical mentorship and knowledge transfer to ITS staff and vendor teams; present architecture strategies, risks, and project updates to leadership. 1 Perform other duties as assigned. Security, Access, Compliance & Risk Management (15%) 1 Review and recommend access models involving profiles, permission sets, permission set groups, sharing rules, role hierarchy, object permissions, field-level security, Experience Cloud users, delegated administration, and internal/external user access patterns. 1 Support design decisions around internal read-only access, external user access, guardian and individual access, provider access, reviewer access, and business-specific role-based access requirements. 1 Support security controls for sensitive data, including PII, PHI, CPI, provider data, individual data, assessment data, files, and other regulated information. 2 Review and advise on security-related changes to page layouts, object permissions, field-level security, record visibility, user administration, community access, and shared object exposure. 2 Support Salesforce security mandate readiness including MFA, IP restrictions, device activation, transaction security policies, DKIM verification, high-risk IP enforcement, and related platform security changes. 2 Identify security and compliance risks caused by shared objects, legacy access patterns, production support changes, page layout changes, or reintroduction of functionality previously removed for PII/PHI risk reasons. Integration, Data Flow & Enterprise Data Architecture (10%) 2 Help teams design reliable upsert patterns using Salesforce IDs, external IDs, SQL identifiers, integration keys, and source-system identifiers. 2 Review data synchronization requirements to prevent duplicate records, stale records, mismatched source systems, unnecessary replication, and unclear source-of-truth ownership. 2 Support architecture decisions involving REST/SOAP APIs, MuleSoft APIs, batch processing, CDC, Platform Events, Event Streamer, event-driven architecture, integration monitoring, correlation IDs, and error handling. 2 Provide guidance on data movement across Salesforce and enterprise systems while balancing operational needs, reporting needs, performance, security, and maintainability. 2 Partner with production and integration teams to perform root cause analysis on complex issues, research solutions, and recommend corrective actions. jobs.title: IAM PAM Program Manager Consultant
jobs.description:
Job Description:
 
Title: IAM PAM Program Manager Consultant
Location: Remote
Duration: 1 year


Role Summary/Purpose:
The Privileged Access Management (PAM) Technical Program Management Consultant will drive execution of Synchrony’s PAM delivery roadmap by leading cross-functional planning, coordination, and delivery governance to bring PAM capabilities into production. This consultant role operates at the intersection of cybersecurity, infrastructure engineering, and enterprise change—owning program plans, eliminating delivery blockers, and ensuring on-time outcomes across complex technical workstreams.
This role will be heavily focused on Delinea, including Delinea Server Suite and platform capabilities, and will manage production readiness challenges such as non-production validation/testing requirements, environment readiness, and firewall/network access requests. The consultant will also facilitate alignment on Just-in-Time (JIT) provisioning and privileged access patterns integrated with SailPoint and Okta.
 
Essential Responsibilities:
• Serve as the technical program management consultant for Synchrony’s PAM initiatives, driving execution across multiple teams, technical dependencies, and timelines.
• Drive delivery of Delinea Server Suite and platform capabilities into production, coordinating engineering, infrastructure, and security stakeholders to progress from implementation/testing to production readiness.
• Manage and resolve program execution challenges and dependencies, including:
o Spinning up Server Suite into the PAM platform and coordinating sequencing, prerequisites, and cutover readiness.
o Navigating scenarios where Server Suite implementation was completed by the Unix team, while AD and other stakeholders require additional validation in non-production prior to production deployment.
o Coordinating and tracking firewall/network access requests and other infrastructure prerequisites required for environment connectivity and integrations.
• Build and maintain an integrated program plan (often Excel-based) capturing milestones, start/finish dates, dependencies, deliverables, and status across all workstreams.
• Establish and maintain a RAID log (Risks, Assumptions, Issues, Dependencies), driving mitigation plans, escalation paths, and closure.
• Lead weekly and/or bi-weekly status meetings, publish concise status reporting, and drive action items to completion with clear owners and due dates.
• Develop and execute a rollout plan and communication plan to ensure stakeholder readiness, training/enablement, and adoption of PAM capabilities.
• Facilitate technical working sessions with engineering leads and SMEs to define and drive JIT provisioning requirements, decisions, and delivery sequencing.
• Partner with Delinea and internal stakeholders to clarify the operating model, including gathering vendor guidance on ideal team structure and supporting the creation of a RACI model for delivery and sustainment.
• Ensure program outcomes align with Synchrony’s security objectives and risk/compliance expectations.
• Assistance with converting all things PIM to PAM

Qualifications/Requirements:
• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience; technology or equivalent related field preferred, with a minimum of 4 years of experience in Information Technology OR in lieu of the Bachelor's degree, a minimum of 6 years of experience in Information Technology.
• 5+ years of experience in technical program management / program delivery supporting cybersecurity, IAM/PAM, infrastructure security, or platform engineering initiatives.
• Demonstrated experience driving execution across cross-functional teams (e.g., IAM, AD, Unix, network, platform engineering, GRC), including managing dependencies and delivery risks.
• Strong understanding of PAM concepts including privileged elevation, vaulting/rotation, privileged session controls, and Just-in-Time (JIT) provisioning approaches.
• Proven ability to create and manage detailed program plans, schedules, RAID logs, and executive-ready status reporting.
• Strong facilitation, conflict resolution, and stakeholder management skills, including the ability to translate technical content for non-technical audiences.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills; highly organized with strong attention to detail.

Desired Characteristics:
• Hands-on delivery familiarity with Delinea, including Server Suite and enterprise PAM platform rollout patterns and production readiness considerations.
• Expertise in JIT provisioning and privileged access, including facilitating requirements, policy alignment, and operational readiness across stakeholders.
• Experience coordinating IAM/PAM ecosystem dependencies and integrations, including SailPoint and Okta.
• Demonstrated ability to drive structured execution using program management artifacts (Excel-based plans, milestone tracking, RAID logs, and recurring governance cadence).
• Comfortable leading weekly/bi-weekly operating rhythms (status meetings, decision forums, dependency reviews) to drive accountability and outcomes.
• Self-starter with a strong sense of urgency and flexibility to change directions quickly.
• Experience in regulated environments (financial services preferred) with awareness of audit, risk management, and control expectations.
• Security certifications (CISSP, CISM, CISA) preferred.

jobs.description:
Job Title: Change Control Lead
Location: Philadelphia, PA
Position Type: Contract 
Duration: 6 / 12 Month
Work Type: Onsite 
Rate: Pay range offered to a successful candidate will be based on several factors, including the candidate's education, work experience, work location, specific job duties, certifications, etc.

Job Description:

 

Technical Skills:
Strong domain knowledge in Video technologies, Set-Top Box platforms, and streaming ecosystems
Good understanding of Networking and WiFi technologies impacting video delivery
Solid understanding of software architecture, system integration, and dependencies across components
Proficiency in Linux environments and familiarity with C/C++ based systems
Experience with monitoring and data analysis tools such as Elastic, Splunk, Datadog, or similar
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to assess risk and impact of changes
Familiarity with software development lifecycle (SDLC), version control systems, and Agile methodologies
Experience with release management, change control processes, and production support
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills across cross-functional teams

Leadership & Behavioral Skills:
Strong decision-making skills, especially under ambiguity and time constraints
Ability to lead change control forums and drive consensus across diverse stakeholders
Proven ability to prioritize competing demands and manage risk effectively
Capability to lead teams, delegate responsibilities, and ensure timely delivery of outcomes
Proactive mindset with a focus on continuous improvement and operational excellence

Key Responsibilities:
As a Change Control Lead, you will be responsible for governing, evaluating, and driving all software and configuration
changes impacting video/set-top box platforms, ensuring stability, quality, and minimal customer impact.
You will lead the change review and approval process by assessing risk, impact, and readiness of proposed changes across video systems, middleware, firmware, and network components.
You will leverage strong analytical thinking to evaluate field issues, proposed fixes, and enhancements, ensuring that only well-vetted and high-quality changes are promoted to production.
You will collaborate closely with triage, development, QA, release management, and operations teams to ensure alignment on priorities, root cause insights, and deployment strategies.
You will drive decision-making during change control boards (CCB), balancing urgency, risk, and business impact while providing clear recommendations.
You will analyze Business Intelligence, telemetry, and field metrics (e.g., crash rates, playback failures, network performance) to proactively identify risks associated with changes and prevent regressions.
You will ensure proper change documentation, traceability, rollback strategies, and compliance with release governance processes.
You will lead incident reviews related to change failures and drive continuous improvement in change management practices.
You will operate in a fast-paced environment, coordinating across multiple teams and stakeholders, ensuring timely and high-quality releases.
You will mentor and guide team members, leveraging team strengths and improving capabilities through training and structured processes.
You will stay current with evolving tools, technologies, and best practices in video platforms, cloud services, monitoring systems, and DevOps methodologies.

What are the Mandatory skills and skill proficiencies required for this position?
Change Control, Networking and Wi-Fi Technologies, Video technologies, Set-Top Box platforms, and streaming ecosystems
